summary.intent: Document the architectural improvement opportunity (unifying folder-state ownership in the SDK client) as a structured GSD todo, following the resolution of PR #489's deterministic web-e2e failure.
summary.outcome: A todo file was created at `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-14-unify-folder-state-ownership-in-sdk-client.md` and committed on an isolated docs branch separate from PR #489, capturing the full bypass-path inventory, proposed projection design, and exit criteria.

repo: Folder state is duplicated across two stores: web Zustand `useFolderStore` (apps/web) and SDK client `folderTree` (packages/sdk/client.ts); they drift when web mutation code calls sdk-core directly rather than routing through the client.
SDK-routed mutations (deleteToBin, move, rename, create) update both folderTree and emit folder:updated → store consistently; bypass paths update only the Zustand store.
The SDK client is also consumed headless by the desktop FUSE mount (no Zustand), making the SDK — not the web store — the correct single source of truth; making the SDK stateless is ruled out.
client.registerFolder has an existing 'gradual SDK adoption bridge' comment, confirming the intent was always to fully own folder loading through the client.
`commit_docs: true` and `.planning/` being tracked means capturing a todo on a feature branch would include it in the PR — requires isolating captures to a separate docs branch.

code.finding: updateFile performs a fire-and-forget '6b' republish that calls sdk-core directly (updateFolderMetadataAndPublish/replaceFileInFolder), bypassing the client and updating only the Zustand store — this is a bypass-path leak.
handleRestoreVersion and handleDeleteVersion (+ lazy IPNS-key migration) also call sdk-core directly, bypassing the SDK client and creating the same desync risk.

reconcileFolderState + ensureFolderRegistered were added in PR #489 as a band-aid reconciliation patch; they become dead code once the full architectural unification is complete and should be deleted as the exit criterion.

workflow: When `.planning/` is git-tracked and you're on a feature branch (e.g. a bugfix PR), capture planning docs on an isolated docs branch to avoid polluting the PR diff.
Before creating a todo, check for duplicates — an adjacent todo about CAS-retry deduplication existed; the new todo was scoped distinctly (state ownership vs code-shape duplication) and cross-linked.
GSD's `commit_docs` config controls whether the tool auto-commits planning files; when true, the capture workflow respects gitignore and only stages specified files.

friction: 1Password was locked throughout the session, making all commits unsigned; PR #489 will show 'Unverified' and may block merge if branch protection requires signed commits.
Capturing a todo required branching off main to avoid leaking planning docs into the open bugfix PR — an extra step not required in a clean-branch context.
The `gsd_run query init.todos` bootstrap command is long and fragile (checks 15+ config paths) — requires the gsd-tools.cjs shim to be locatable.
open_items: Medium multi-PR architectural refactor: convert bypass paths (useFileOperations.updateFile, useFileVersions.handleRestoreVersion/handleDeleteVersion) into SDK client methods (client.replaceFile, client.updateFileMetadata) that own publish + sequence bookkeeping + folder:updated emission.
Make useFolderStore a projection: children/sequenceNumber written only via folder:updated events, never by web mutation code.
Delete client.reconcileFolderState once the full refactor lands (it becomes dead code; desync is impossible by construction).
Residual sub-second race in PR #489: a delete can fire between a replace's publish landing and its .then updating the store seq — TC08's 3s wait hides it but it remains real.
Re-sign the PR #489 commit once 1Password is unlocked: `git commit --amend --no-edit -S && git push --force-with-lease`.
